subject: Renewal uplift — staged credit pockets and co-term path
messages:
From: Samuel Tan <samuel.tan@novamed.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Mid-contract capacity add + co-term question

Hi Rachel,

Quick one — Q2 usage has spiked (~2.6x month-over-month) and the team expects sustained higher inference volume for the next 6–9 months. We're evaluating an immediate capacity top-up and would like to co-term the added capacity with our existing Jan renewal instead of paying two invoices.

Can you outline options for:
- pricing on an immediate top-up (monthly billing) vs annualizing now,
- whether you can apply a credit buffer / staged credit to smooth the invoice impact, and
- any procurement requirements or PO language we should prepare for legal?

Attaching the Q2 usage extract for your planning. Procurement also looped in (procurement@novamed.com).

Thanks —
Sam
Samuel Tan
Head of Platform, Novamed
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Tan <samuel.tan@novamed.com>
Cc: procurement@novamed.com
Date: 2027-06-10T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-contract capacity add + co-term question

Sam — thanks for the data. Confirming receipt of the CSV. Below are three workable paths (short summary + next steps). I tried to keep procurement implications minimal.

1) Immediate top-up (monthly billing, fastest)
   - Price: standard top-up rate = base list * 1.0 (no annual discount);
   - Smooth option: we can apply a staged credit pocket equal to 30% of the first 3 months' overage, distributed as monthly vouchers to offset invoices;
   - Procurement: PO referencing "Redwood Inference Order Form v1" + short amendment for top-up.

2) Early annualize (move added capacity onto the contract now)
   - Price: blended annual rate (approx ~8% discount vs top-up list) if you commit the added monthly baseline for 12 months;
   - Benefit: single invoice cadence and easier cost predictability for your finance team.

3) Hybrid (recommended for risk smoothing)
   - Commit to a 6-month bridging credit: 50% of the projected incremental usage for months 1–3 as voucher credits, then reassess; if you elect to annualize within 90 days, we convert vouchers into a pre-paid portion of the annualized commit and apply a 5% conversion credit.

What I need from you:
- preferred path (Immediate / Annualize / Hybrid),
- confirmation of PO timeline (PO within 30 days to lock in the quoted top-up rate),
- any internal approval constraints (finance or security must sign the amendment).

I'm attaching a draft SLA amendment that legal can pre-review (SLA-Amendment_v2.pdf) and the usage extract you sent. If you'd like, I can run a 6-month invoice simulation to show expected cashflow.

Best,
Rachel
Rachel Kim

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Mid-contract capacity add + co-term question — approval request

Ben / Neha — forwarding Novamed's ask and the usage extract. Proposal I'd like to offer (customer-friendly, preserves economics):

- Offer path: Hybrid (recommended)
  * 30% voucher credit applied to the first 3 monthly top-up invoices (reduces sticker shock);
  * Option to annualize within 90 days — if they annualize, convert unused vouchers into pre-paid committed units and apply a 5% conversion credit;
  * If annualize immediately, we can offer an 8% blended discount on the added capacity.

- Constraints / ask of finance: cap total discount exposure to 8% for account-level approval; require PO within 30 days of quote to lock rates.

Estimated P&L impact (back-of-envelope):
- Current ARR footprint: ~$230k / year for their baseline;
- Incremental run-rate if they sustain spike: +$85k/month;
- 30% voucher over 3 months ~= $76.5k gross offset (applied across invoices); converted into annualized commit could partially prepay ~3–4 months of usage.

Please confirm if finance can approve up to 8% discount and voucher approach; legal will need to sign the SLA amendment (attached). If you're comfortable, I'll present the Hybrid + conversion option to Samuel and procurement. HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/4201

Thanks —
Rachel

1) Discount ceiling: 8% maximum on any converted annualized amount.
2) Voucher pool: allow the 30% staged-credit pocket for first 3 months, but require a hard cap equal to 110% of the projected incremental usage to avoid open-ended liability.
3) PO requirement: PO or signed amendment within 30 days to lock pricing.

If legal can get the SLA amendment updated to include the PO clause, proceed to present the Hybrid + conversion option to Novamed. Mark the deal as DEAL-4201 and attach the SLA amendment via DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/en/execute/AMENDMENT-4201
